title: The map from the zig-zag module to the homology of the row-cokernel complex
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $A=(A_{p,q},d,\delta)_{p,q\ge0}$ be a homological double complex of $R$-modules: $R$-modules $A_{p,q}$ ($p,q\ge0$) and $R$-linear maps $d_{p,q}:A_{p,q}\to A_{p-1,q}$ ($p\ge1$) and $\delta_{p,q}:A_{p,q}\to A_{p,q-1}$ ($q\ge1$) with $d_{p-1,q}\circ d_{p,q}=0$, $\delta_{p,q-1}\circ\delta_{p,q}=0$ and $\delta_{p-1,q}\circ d_{p,q}=d_{p,q-1}\circ\delta_{p,q}$ whenever defined; put $A_{p,q}=0$ if $p<0$ or $q<0$ and let $d_{0,q}$, $\delta_{p,0}$ and all maps out of or into a zero module be $0$. A morphism $\Phi:A\to B$ of such double complexes is a family of $R$-linear maps $\Phi_{p,q}:A_{p,q}\to B_{p,q}$ with $\Phi d=d\Phi$ and $\Phi\delta=\delta\Phi$. Let $A^{\mathrm{rt}}_q=\operatorname{Coker}(d_{1,q}:A_{1,q}\to A_{0,q})$ with projection $\pi_q:A_{0,q}\to A^{\mathrm{rt}}_q$ ($q\ge0$); since $\delta_{0,q}(\operatorname{im}d_{1,q})=d_{1,q-1}(\delta_{1,q}(A_{1,q}))\subseteq\operatorname{im}d_{1,q-1}$, the map $\delta_{0,q}$ induces $\delta^{\mathrm{rt}}_q:A^{\mathrm{rt}}_q\to A^{\mathrm{rt}}_{q-1}$ with $\delta^{\mathrm{rt}}_q\pi_q=\pi_{q-1}\delta_{0,q}$ ($q\ge1$), and $A^{\mathrm{rt}}_\bullet$ is a chain complex of $R$-modules concentrated in degrees $\ge0$ [def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology]; a morphism $\Phi$ induces the morphism of complexes $\Phi^{\mathrm{rt}}$ with $\Phi^{\mathrm{rt}}_q\pi_q=\pi_q\Phi_{0,q}$. Let $Z_n(A)\subseteq T_n(A)=\bigoplus_{p+q=n}A_{p,q}$ and $B_n(A)\subseteq T_n(A)$ be the modules of zig-zags and of trivial zig-zags of total degree $n$ [def-weil-pbc-double-complex-zigzag-module]. Then for every $n\ge0$: (a) for every $a\in Z_n(A)$ the element $\pi_n(a_{0,n})$ is a cycle of $A^{\mathrm{rt}}_\bullet$ (i.e. $n=0$ or $\delta^{\mathrm{rt}}_n(\pi_n(a_{0,n}))=0$); (b) for every $a\in Z_n(A)\cap B_n(A)$ the class of $\pi_n(a_{0,n})$ in $H_n(A^{\mathrm{rt}}_\bullet)$ is zero. Hence $a\mapsto[\pi_n(a_{0,n})]$ induces an $R$-linear map $\rho^A_n:\mathbf H_n(A)\to H_n(A^{\mathrm{rt}}_\bullet)$ on the zig-zag module $\mathbf H_n(A)=Z_n(A)/(Z_n(A)\cap B_n(A))$. (c) For every morphism $\Phi:A\to B$ of double complexes, $H_n(\Phi^{\mathrm{rt}})\circ\rho^A_n=\rho^B_n\circ\mathbf H_n(\Phi)$, where $\mathbf H_n(\Phi)$ is the map of [def-weil-pbc-double-complex-zigzag-module]. No exactness of rows or columns is assumed.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00M1 (lemma-no-spectral-sequence), tag verified in tags/tags (00M1,algebra-lemma-no-spectral-sequence); proof, lines 18449-18461: 'Note that there are canonical homomorphisms $\mathbf H_i(A)\to H_i(R(A)_\bullet)$, $(a_{i,0},\dots,a_{0,i})\mapsto$ class of image of $a_{0,i}$' (well-definedness not written in the source), and lines 18506-18521 (the commutative diagram of the functoriality paragraph)

proof.text: (The row-cokernel complex and $\Phi^{\mathrm{rt}}$.) For $x\in A_{1,q}$ ($q\ge1$), $\delta_{0,q}(d_{1,q}x)=d_{1,q-1}(\delta_{1,q}x)\in\operatorname{im}d_{1,q-1}$, so $\pi_{q-1}\circ\delta_{0,q}$ vanishes on $\operatorname{im}d_{1,q}=\ker\pi_q$ and factors uniquely through the surjection $\pi_q$ as an $R$-linear $\delta^{\mathrm{rt}}_q$ with $\delta^{\mathrm{rt}}_q\pi_q=\pi_{q-1}\delta_{0,q}$. Then $\delta^{\mathrm{rt}}_{q-1}\delta^{\mathrm{rt}}_q\pi_q=\pi_{q-2}\delta_{0,q-1}\delta_{0,q}=0$ and $\pi_q$ is surjective, so $\delta^{\mathrm{rt}}_{q-1}\delta^{\mathrm{rt}}_q=0$ and $A^{\mathrm{rt}}_\bullet$ (extended by $0$ in negative degrees, $\delta^{\mathrm{rt}}_0=0$) is a chain complex in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology]. For a morphism $\Phi$: $\Phi_{0,q}(d_{1,q}x)=d_{1,q}(\Phi_{1,q}x)$, so $\pi_q\Phi_{0,q}$ vanishes on $\ker\pi_q$ and defines $\Phi^{\mathrm{rt}}_q$ with $\Phi^{\mathrm{rt}}_q\pi_q=\pi_q\Phi_{0,q}$; and $\delta^{\mathrm{rt}}_q\Phi^{\mathrm{rt}}_q\pi_q=\pi_{q-1}\delta_{0,q}\Phi_{0,q}=\pi_{q-1}\Phi_{0,q-1}\delta_{0,q}=\Phi^{\mathrm{rt}}_{q-1}\delta^{\mathrm{rt}}_q\pi_q$, so by surjectivity of $\pi_q$ the family $\Phi^{\mathrm{rt}}$ is a morphism of chain complexes, which induces $H_n(\Phi^{\mathrm{rt}})$ [def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology]. (This verifies the facts the statement records about $A^{\mathrm{rt}}_\bullet$ and $\Phi^{\mathrm{rt}}$; the source calls them clear.)

source.place: Algebra, the paragraph before Lemma 00M1 (lines 18390-18394): 'it is clear that this induces morphisms of complexes $R(\Phi)$'; $R(A)_j=\operatorname{Coker}(A_{1,j}\to A_{0,j})$ is $A^{\mathrm{rt}}_j$ here

proof.text: (a) Let $a\in Z_n(A)$. If $n=0$ there is nothing to prove ($\delta^{\mathrm{rt}}_0=0$). If $n\ge1$, the zig-zag condition of [def-weil-pbc-double-complex-zigzag-module] at $(p,q)=(1,n-1)$ reads $d_{1,n-1}(a_{1,n-1})=\delta_{0,n}(a_{0,n})$. Hence $\delta^{\mathrm{rt}}_n(\pi_n(a_{0,n}))=\pi_{n-1}(\delta_{0,n}(a_{0,n}))=\pi_{n-1}(d_{1,n-1}(a_{1,n-1}))=0$, since $\pi_{n-1}$ kills $\operatorname{im}d_{1,n-1}$. So $\pi_n(a_{0,n})\in\ker\delta^{\mathrm{rt}}_n$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00M1 (lemma-no-spectral-sequence), proof, lines 18449-18455: the canonical homomorphism $\mathbf H_i(A)\to H_i(R(A)_\bullet)$, zig-zag $\mapsto$ class of image of $a_{0,i}$ (the cycle property is not written in the source)

proof.text: (b) Let $a\in Z_n(A)\cap B_n(A)$. By [def-weil-pbc-double-complex-zigzag-module], $a=D_{n+1}(b)$ for some $b\in T_{n+1}(A)$, so its component at $(0,n)$ is $a_{0,n}=d_{1,n}(b_{1,n})+\delta_{0,n+1}(b_{0,n+1})$. Applying $\pi_n$ and using $\pi_n d_{1,n}=0$ and $\pi_n\delta_{0,n+1}=\delta^{\mathrm{rt}}_{n+1}\pi_{n+1}$ (step 1) gives $\pi_n(a_{0,n})=\delta^{\mathrm{rt}}_{n+1}(\pi_{n+1}(b_{0,n+1}))\in\operatorname{im}\delta^{\mathrm{rt}}_{n+1}$; by (a) it lies in $\ker\delta^{\mathrm{rt}}_n$, and its class in $H_n(A^{\mathrm{rt}}_\bullet)=\ker\delta^{\mathrm{rt}}_n/\operatorname{im}\delta^{\mathrm{rt}}_{n+1}$ [def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology] is zero.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00M1 (lemma-no-spectral-sequence), proof, lines 18438-18450 (trivial zig-zags; 'we divide out by trivial zig-zags') and the converse direction used in lines 18484-18491 ('$a_{0,i}$ is in the image of $\delta\oplus d:A_{0,i+1}\oplus A_{1,i}\to A_{0,i}$'); the well-definedness itself is not written in the source

proof.text: (The map $\rho^A_n$.) The map $\tilde\rho:Z_n(A)\to H_n(A^{\mathrm{rt}}_\bullet)$, $a\mapsto[\pi_n(a_{0,n})]$, is the composite of the $R$-linear maps $Z_n(A)\hookrightarrow T_n(A)\to A_{0,n}$ (projection to the component $(0,n)$), $\pi_n$, which lands in $\ker\delta^{\mathrm{rt}}_n$ on $Z_n(A)$ by (a), and the quotient map $\ker\delta^{\mathrm{rt}}_n\to H_n(A^{\mathrm{rt}}_\bullet)$; hence it is $R$-linear. By (b) its kernel contains the submodule $Z_n(A)\cap B_n(A)$, so by the universal property of the quotient module it factors uniquely through $\mathbf H_n(A)=Z_n(A)/(Z_n(A)\cap B_n(A))$ as an $R$-linear map $\rho^A_n$ with $\rho^A_n([a])=[\pi_n(a_{0,n})]$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00M1 (lemma-no-spectral-sequence), proof, lines 18449-18455 ('Note that there are canonical homomorphisms $\mathbf H_i(A)\to H_i(R(A)_\bullet)$')

proof.text: (c) Let $\Phi:A\to B$ and $[a]\in\mathbf H_n(A)$ with $a\in Z_n(A)$. By [def-weil-pbc-double-complex-zigzag-module], $\mathbf H_n(\Phi)[a]=[\Phi(a)]$ with $\Phi(a)_{0,n}=\Phi_{0,n}(a_{0,n})$, so $\rho^B_n(\mathbf H_n(\Phi)[a])=[\pi_n(\Phi_{0,n}(a_{0,n}))]=[\Phi^{\mathrm{rt}}_n(\pi_n(a_{0,n}))]$ by step 1, and this is $H_n(\Phi^{\mathrm{rt}})([\pi_n(a_{0,n})])=H_n(\Phi^{\mathrm{rt}})(\rho^A_n[a])$ by the definition of the induced map on homology [def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology]. As every element of $\mathbf H_n(A)$ is such a class, $H_n(\Phi^{\mathrm{rt}})\circ\rho^A_n=\rho^B_n\circ\mathbf H_n(\Phi)$. No exactness of rows or columns was used in steps 1-5.

lean.note: The row-cokernel chain complex is the existing Mathlib HomologicalComplex.opcycles of the outer complex in degree zero. The existential natural family is uniquely specified on zig-zag representatives; no duplicate cokernel or homology notion is introduced.
